notes.title: BESSELI is ITK's published polynomial and recurrence, on the x87 unit
notes.statement: BESSELI truncates n to an integer and evaluates the body published in ITK with every operation stored from the x87 unit at precision 64: the I0 and I1 polynomials, and for higher orders Miller backward recurrence from j = 2*(n + int(sqrt(40*n))), rescaling by 1E-10 whenever |q| > 1E10, then normalising by I0(x). The same body in plain binary64 misses by 1 to 4 units in the last place. The published ITK body is itkGaussianOperator.hxx at ITK 311b7060ef39e371f3cd209ec135284ff5fde735 (Apache-2.0).

notes.title: Small arguments evaluate x*N(t)/D(t) on the x87 unit with stored steps, and the last bit can be high
notes.statement: For normal x with |x| < 2^-16, ERF.PRECISE computes x*N(t)/D(t) with t = x^2 on the x87 unit at precision 64: N and D are each stored to binary64, then the product, then the quotient. Below 2^-27 this reduces to p = RN53(RN64(x*P0)) and y = RN53(RN64(p/Q0)), with P0 = 0x3ff1df5e70c7956b and Q0 = 0x3fefada15778ece6. The coefficient table is unidentified: Cody's 1969 rational shares the constant-term ratio, as any accurate table does, but its normalised linear terms differ (0.1176 and 0.4510 against Excel's 0.1259 and 0.4593), and Cephes and fdlibm also miss. The rounded steps can leave the answer 1 unit above the correctly rounded erf(x), as the rows below show. The same route explains GAUSS's small arguments.
notes.basis: All 499,814 recorded ERF.PRECISE rows with 0 < |x| < 2^-16 match; per-operation binary64 misses rows in the 2^-40 binade alone (131,201 of 131,255). Bisecting live Excel to one input ulp located where stored D and stored N first step, and every answer fit those two hypotheses. The measured coefficients give N1/N0 - D1/D0 = -1/3 to 1.2e-16, which is erf's Taylor coefficient and was not imposed by the measurement.
notes.inferred: That the legacy ERF(x) shares this body is inferred; only ERF.PRECISE and GAUSS rows were scored. D1 is one of two adjacent values that no recorded answer separates.

notes.title: MROUND counts a quotient within 5E-15 below a half up
notes.statement: MROUND(n,m) forms q = n/m on the x87 unit, counts floor(q), adds 1 when 0.5 - frac(q) <= 5E-15, and returns count*m from the x87 unit. A number just below a half therefore rounds up though it is nearer the lower multiple: 0.499999999999995 with multiple 1 gives 1, and the next binary64 below it gives 0. MROUND(6.05,0.1) stays 6, because its quotient 60.49999999999999 lies 7.1E-15 below the half.
notes.basis: All 50,782 recorded MROUND rows match this rule. The cut-off lies between the adjacent binary64 values 4.996E-15 (rounded up) and 5.0515E-15 (rounded down) from 0.5, measured at floor(q) = 0 over 4,264 rows.
notes.inferred: The window is measured between two neighbouring values; that the constant is the decimal 5E-15 is inferred, as the decimal in that window.

documentation.claim: MROUND rounds up, away from zero, if the remainder of dividing number by multiple is greater than or equal to half the value of multiple.

notes.title: PMT stores the quotient before it multiplies by the rate
notes.statement: With fv 0, type 0 and rate > 0, PMT's last two steps are q = RN53(RN64(pv/em)) then RN53(RN64(q*rate)): the x87 unit at precision 64, each result stored to binary64, where em = (1+rate)^-nper - 1 is a stored binary64. Holding one free binary64 em for each (rate, nper), this order admits a consistent em in all 4,802 bank groups with 8 or more pv values. A binary64 quotient leaves 59 groups with no em, and binary64 for both steps 111. The three other orders tested (rate/em, pv*rate then /em, em/rate) fit only 8 to 12 of 40 sampled groups. notes.title: ROUND counts digits in 32 bits, and the count wraps
notes.statement: ROUND cuts num_digits toward zero to a 32-bit integer D, limited to +/-2147483647, and keeps k = D + e + 1 significant digits, where e is the decimal exponent of |number| and the sum is computed in 32 bits. k of 15 or more keeps the 15-digit reading of the number; k below 0 gives 0. A large positive num_digits therefore wraps to no digits at all: for a number near 1.1E14, 2147483617 returns the number and 2147483635 returns 0. The boundaries move by exactly -e on both the +2^31 and -2^31 sides, for e from -308 to 308. num_digits of 2^31 or more acts as +2147483647 and -2^31 or less as -2147483647.
notes.basis: Under the family rules the OxFunc-Evidence bank matches ROUND 36,391 of 36,945 rows, ROUNDUP 49,013 of 52,841, ROUNDDOWN 59,080 of 59,995 and TRUNC 50,409 of 51,317, with no row lost and each remaining failure classified in the write-up. The wrap boundary was read at every decimal exponent in the bank.

correct.how: -112500000000000 is an integer, so rounding it to any non-negative number of places returns it.

notes.title: The rounding functions read 15 digits first, so ROUNDDOWN can round up
notes.statement: Before choosing a digit these functions read the number to 15 significant digits on the x87 unit: with e the decimal exponent and n = 14 - e, y = RN64(|x| * 10^n), or RN64(|x| / 10^-n) when n is negative, while 10^|n| is exact in 64 bits (|n| <= 27). A half in y goes up for ROUNDDOWN, ROUNDUP and TRUNC and down for ROUND. So digits beyond the 15th are lost even when the requested precision keeps them: ROUND(-1594628480062905,14) loses its last digit, and ROUNDDOWN(283025097725723.5,0) returns 283025097725724, larger than its input.

notes.title: Near DBL_MAX, ROUND returns NaN bit patterns that Excel treats as numbers
notes.statement: ROUND of a number near 1.8E308 can return a binary64 with an all-ones exponent field: the decimal-to-binary conversion does not saturate, and a value of 1.8E308 comes out with the exponent overflowed. The bank holds 430 such ROUND rows, 102 ROUNDDOWN and 95 TRUNC. Even ROUND(DBL_MAX,0), whose answer is DBL_MAX, returns 0x7ff000000000000a. The cell shows 2E+308 or 1.8E+308, ISNUMBER gives TRUE, ISERROR FALSE, TYPE 1, and =A1, N(A1), MAX(A1), ABS(A1) and IFERROR(A1,...) pass the pattern on, as does =-A1 with its sign unchanged. Arithmetic on it (A1+0, A1*1, A1-A1, SUM, ROUND) gives #NUM!, TEXT(A1,"0") gives #VALUE!, ERROR.TYPE(A1) gives #N/A. Saved to .xlsx and reopened, the cells read #NUM! until recalculated, when the patterns return.
notes.basis: One Excel workbook read cell by cell through Value2 on 2026-11-04, saved, reopened and recalculated; bank counts from the rounding write-up.

notes.title: ROUNDUP, ROUNDDOWN and TRUNC read num_digits from its low 16 bits
notes.statement: ROUNDUP, ROUNDDOWN and TRUNC take the digit count from the low 16 bits of the integer part of |num_digits|, with the sign of num_digits. If |num_digits| is 2^32 or more, or those low bits are 32768 or more, the truncation happens at 100 places (10^-100, or 10^100 for a negative count). So 65536 acts as 0, 65537 as 1, 32768 to 65535 as 100, and -2147483748, whose low 16 bits are 100, as -100. In the out-of-range case ROUNDUP adds no unit for a positive count, and gives #NUM! for a negative count when a digit is dropped.
notes.basis: Under the family rules the OxFunc-Evidence bank matches ROUND 36,391 of 36,945 rows, ROUNDUP 49,013 of 52,841, ROUNDDOWN 59,080 of 59,995 and TRUNC 50,409 of 51,317, with no row lost and each remaining failure classified in the write-up. All 13,914 informative ROUNDDOWN and TRUNC rows with large num_digits follow the rule.

correct.how: The exact decimal expansion of this binary64 number has fewer than 32768 places, so a truncation at num_digits places returns the number itself.

notes.title: ROUNDUP adds its unit in binary64, one bit from the decimal answer
notes.statement: ROUNDUP forms the ROUNDDOWN result, converts it to binary64, converts one unit 10^-p to binary64, and adds the two in binary64. The sum need not be the binary64 value nearest the decimal answer, so ROUNDUP(-1.125,2) is -1.1300000000000001 and ROUNDUP(3.535,2) is 3.5399999999999996. The difference shows when the result is compared with a typed 3.54.

notes.statement: The worksheet SQRT is RN53(RN64(sqrt(x))): the root is rounded to the x87 unit's 64-bit significand and then stored to binary64. notes.title: For bills longer than 182 days TBILLEQ is a quadratic, not the documented formula
notes.statement: When DSM is above 182, TBILLEQ does not use the documented formula. It uses the bond-equivalent quadratic (-t + sqrt(t^2 - (2t-1)(1 - 1/p))) / (t - 1/2), with t = DSM/365 and p = price/100. The square root is taken in extended precision and stored, RN53(RN64(sqrt)); the rest is binary64. For the row below, DSM 203, the documented formula gives 0.244038 and Excel 0.241103. Excel's bits are 22 units below the correctly rounded quadratic because of that staging.
notes.basis: 2,400 of 2,400 recorded rows with the stored square root; 2,399 without it.

documentation.claim: TBILLEQ is calculated as TBILLEQ = (365 x rate)/(360-(rate x DSM)); the page does not mention 182 days.

correct.how: mpmath at 800 bits: the exact quadratic at the binary64 inputs, correctly rounded.

notes.title: Locale-tagged month, weekday and era names in TEXT follow their own table
notes.statement: With a locale tag in the format, TEXT's names differ from common locale data. [$-407] (German) gives mmm for March as Mrz, while mmmm gives März. [$-411] (Japanese) gives mmm as a bare number, 1, while mmmm gives 1月. [$-419] (Russian) capitalises mmmm (Январь) but not mmm (янв), and capitalises ddd (Ср) but not dddd. The first year of the Reiwa era prints as 1, not 元年; g, gg and ggg give R, 令 and 令和, switching on 2019-05-01.
notes.basis: 170 recorded TEXT readings on the fn3_text sheet.

notes.statement: With DBL_MIN (0x0010000000000000) as number, TRUNC, ROUNDDOWN and ROUNDUP return the subnormal 0x000ffffffffffffa at each num_digits recorded, so TRUNC(DBL_MIN,0) is not 0. notes.title: An empty factor slot in VDB is 0, not the default 2
notes.statement: VDB defaults factor to 2 only when the argument is left off the end of the call. An empty slot, as in VDB(c,s,l,a,b,,FALSE), is read as 0, and the result is the straight-line amount: 90 here, where factor 2 gives 160. Text factors other than numbers give #VALUE!, including "TRUE" and "FALSE", while "2" is read as 2.
notes.basis: Ten recorded option readings (cases 00022 to 00031 of the run). After the change VDB matches 142 of 142 retained padding calls.
